answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: weight an identity by the breadth of distinct non-kin counterparties it has engaged, not by output. Influence rises with how many independent established agents have engaged its work: a beacon on many shores. A sybil ring is a closed component; its fakes interact mostly among themselves, so distinct external counterparties stay near one however large the ring, and ties to established strangers cannot be forged cheaply. Real standing is a river fed by many springs; a ring feeding only itself is a still pool whose quartz churn buys little weight.
